questions.question: The mob-burning of a police station in Chauri Chaura in 1922 brought about the end of the Non-Cooperation Movement. In which present-day state is Chauri Chaura located?

• The Chauri Chaura incident took place on February 4, 1922, during the Non-Cooperation Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• In this incident, a large group of protesters clashed with the police, leading to the police station being set on fire and resulting in the deaths of 22 policemen.
 
• This incident led Mahatma Gandhi to call off the Non-Cooperation Movement, as he did not want the movement to turn violent.

• It was a significant movement in the Indian independence struggle, led by Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian National Congress.
 
• The movement aimed to resist British rule in India through non-violent means or "satyagraha".
 
• It involved the refusal to buy British goods, the boycott of British educational institutions and legal courts, and the resignation from government employment.
 
• The movement was launched on September 4, 1920, and was called off by Gandhi in February 1922 following the Chauri Chaura incident.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi:**
 
 
• He was an Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, and political ethicist who led the successful campaign for India's independence from British rule.
 
• Gandhi is widely recognized for his philosophy of non-violence (ahimsa) and his method of peaceful protest (satyagraha).

questions.question: What is the general circulation of the atmosphere?

options.text: The pattern of the movement of the surface winds.
The pattern of the movement of the planetary winds.
The pattern of the movement of the water.
The pattern of the movement of the energy.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the pattern of the movement of the planetary winds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The general circulation of the atmosphere refers to the large-scale movement of air through the planet's troposphere.
 
• It encompasses the global patterns of wind that are primarily driven by the uneven heating of the Earth's surface.
 
• These wind patterns are responsible for the distribution of heat and moisture around the globe.
 
• Understanding these patterns is crucial for predicting weather and climate changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmospheric Circulation:**

 
 
• Atmospheric circulation is the large-scale movement of air and the means by which thermal energy is distributed on the surface of the Earth.
 
• The Earth's rotation and the differential heating of its surface cause the formation of distinct wind patterns.
 
 
 
• **Hadley Cell:**
 
 
• The Hadley cell is a tropical atmospheric circulation that features rising motion near the equator, poleward flow 10–15 kilometers above the surface, descending motion in the subtropics, and equatorward flow near the surface.
 
• It plays a key role in the trade winds, tropical rain belts, and subtropical deserts.
 
 
 
• **Ferrel Cell:**
 
 
• The Ferrel cell is the mid-latitude segment of Earth's wind circulation, featuring air rising at low pressure areas around 60° latitude and sinking at high pressure areas around 30° latitude.
 
• This cell is characterized by prevailing westerlies.
 
 
 
• **Polar Cell:**
 
 
• The polar cell is the smallest and weakest atmospheric circulation cell, which extends from 60° latitude to the poles.
 
• Cold air sinks at the poles and flows equatorward at the surface, causing the polar easterlies.

questions.question: The term ‘secular’ was added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act in the year ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term 'secular' was added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act in the year **1976**.
 
• This amendment is also known as the **Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976**.
 
• The 42nd Amendment is one of the most comprehensive amendments made to the Indian Constitution.
 
• The amendment emphasized the **democratic and secular fabric** of the Indian state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Secularism**

 
 
• Secularism in the Indian context means that the state shall not discriminate against any citizen on the basis of religion and treats all religions with equal respect.
 
• It ensures that individuals have the freedom to practice, profess, and propagate any religion of their choice.
 
• In India, it also means the separation of religion from political, economic, social, and cultural spheres of life.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• This amendment is known for its **extensive changes** to the Constitution, often referred to as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging modifications.
 
• Besides adding the term "secular", it also added the term "socialist" to the Preamble.
 
• It laid down Fundamental Duties of citizens under Part IV-A (Article 51A).
 
• It attempted to reduce the power of the judiciary and increase the power of the Parliament and the executive.
 
 
 
• **Preamble of the Indian Constitution**
 
 
• The Preamble is an introductory statement that sets out the guiding purposes and principles of the Constitution.
 
• It declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.
 
• The Preamble outlines the objectives of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• Although it is not enforceable by law, it is a crucial guide to the interpretation of the Constitution.

questions.question: During the Mughal period, what were the farmers called who cultivate their own land?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khud Kashta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Khud Kashta were farmers who **cultivated their own land** during the Mughal period.
 
• They were different from Pahi Kashtas who **cultivated the land of others** and were often tenants or sharecroppers.
 
• Khud Kashta farmers were typically **more stable and had more rights** over the land compared to other categories of farmers.
 
• They were crucial to the agrarian economy of the Mughal Empire, contributing significantly to agricultural production and tax revenues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zamindar**

 
 
• Zamindars were landlords or aristocrats in the Indian subcontinent who held large tracts of land and controlled the peasants.
 
• They were responsible for collecting taxes from the farmers and paying them to the Mughal administration.
 
• They often had significant local power and influence.
 
 
 
• **Muzarain**
 
 
• Muzarain refers to tenant farmers or sharecroppers who cultivated land owned by Zamindars or other landlords.
 
• They were typically less secure than Khud Kashta farmers and had to give a portion of their produce as rent.
 
• Their status and security were dependent on the policies and practices of the landlords.
 
 
 
• **Pahi Kasht**
 
 
• Pahi Kasht were non-resident cultivators who worked on the land of others, often on a temporary or seasonal basis.
 
• They were usually migrants or laborers who did not own land and had less stability compared to Khud Kashta farmers.
 
• They moved from one place to another in search of work and could be evicted more easily by landlords.

questions.question: In which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress was the demand for ‘Swaraj’ put forward for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcutta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The demand for 'Swaraj' was first put forward in the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906.
 
• This session was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, who was a prominent leader and played a significant role in the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• The term 'Swaraj' means self-rule or self-governance, and it marked a significant shift in the Indian National Congress's approach towards the British rule.
 
• The Calcutta session of 1906 laid the foundation for the future struggle for complete independence from British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

 
 
• The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in 1885 and played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement against British rule.
 
• It was initially a platform for educated Indians to discuss and address issues related to British policies and governance.
 
• Over the years, INC evolved into a mass movement demanding complete independence (Purna Swaraj) from British rule.
 
• Key leaders of the INC included Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Subhas Chandra Bose, and many others who played pivotal roles in India's struggle for freedom.
 
 
 
• **Swaraj**
 
 
• Swaraj is a Sanskrit term meaning 'self-rule' or 'self-governance'.
 
• It was a fundamental concept in the Indian independence movement, advocating for India's right to govern itself without foreign interference.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi popularized the term and used it extensively in his campaigns and writings, emphasizing the need for moral and ethical governance.
 
• Swaraj also encompassed social and economic self-reliance, urging Indians to boycott British goods and promote indigenous industries.
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**
 
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji was a prominent Indian nationalist leader, educator, and economist.
 
• He was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress and served as its president three times.
 
• Naoroji was the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament, where he advocated for Indian rights and self-governance.
 
• He is known for his work on the economic drain theory, which highlighted how British colonial policies were leading to the impoverishment of India.
 
 
 
• **Calcutta Session of 1906**
 
 
• The Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906 was a significant event in the Indian freedom movement.
 
• It marked the beginning of a more assertive phase in the Congress's demand for self-governance and laid the groundwork for future movements for independence.
 
• The session was attended by prominent leaders, including Dadabhai Naoroji, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal.
 
• The resolution for Swaraj passed during this session was a turning point, signaling the Congress's commitment to achieving self-rule for India.

questions.question: Tippani is a well-known dance of which of the following states?

• Tippani is a famous traditional dance form of **Gujarat**, India.

questions.question: Where is the headquarter of the WTO located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Geneva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The World Trade Organization (WTO) is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
 
• The WTO officially commenced on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement, replacing the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), which commenced in 1948.
 
• The organization deals with the global rules of trade between nations and aims to ensure that trade flows as smoothly, predictably, and freely as possible.
 
• It currently has 164 member states, representing over 98% of world trade, and its top decision-making body is the Ministerial Conference which meets every two years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT):**

 
 
• GATT was a legal agreement between many countries, whose overall purpose was to promote international trade by reducing or eliminating trade barriers such as tariffs or quotas.
 
• It was signed by 23 nations in Geneva on October 30, 1947, and took effect on January 1, 1948.
 
• GATT remained in effect until the establishment of the WTO in 1995.
 
 
 
• **Marrakesh Agreement:**
 
 
• The Marrakesh Agreement, also known as the Marrakesh Agreement Establishing the World Trade Organization, was signed in Marrakesh, Morocco on 15 April 1994.
 
• The agreement marked the culmination of the Uruguay Round of General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) negotiations.
 
• This agreement led to the creation of the WTO, which took over the responsibilities of GATT in managing international trade.
 
 
 
• **Ministerial Conference:**
 
 
• The Ministerial Conference is the topmost decision-making body of the WTO and meets at least once every two years.
 
• It brings together all members of the WTO, all of which are countries or customs unions.
 
• The conference can take decisions on all matters under any of the multilateral trade agreements.
 
 
 
• **WTO Membership:**
 
 
• As of 2023, the WTO has 164 member states and 25 observer governments.
 
• Members of the WTO are required to follow its rules and regulations, which cover various aspects of international trade.
 
• The accession process for new members involves a detailed examination of the applicant's trade and economic policies.

questions.question: Which genus of the Rhodophyceae family possesses an erect series of branches and a filamentous prostrate section attached to the substratum by means of unicellular rhizoids?

The correct answer is __**Polysiphonia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Polysiphonia is a genus of red algae (Rhodophyceae) known for its complex life cycle and filamentous structure.
 
• It possesses an erect series of branches and a filamentous prostrate section attached to the substratum by means of unicellular rhizoids.
 
• The genus is typically found in marine environments, often in intertidal zones and shallow waters.
 
• Polysiphonia species are important for studying the reproductive biology and development of red algae.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rhodophyceae (Red Algae)**

 
 
• Rhodophyceae is a class of the division Rhodophyta, commonly known as red algae.
 
• They are primarily marine algae, although some freshwater species exist.
 
• Red algae are characterized by the presence of the pigment phycoerythrin, which gives them their distinctive red color.
 
• They play a significant role in marine ecosystems, contributing to the formation of coral reefs and serving as a food source for various marine organisms.
 
 
 
• **Unicellular Rhizoids**
 
 
• Rhizoids are root-like structures found in some algae and non-vascular plants.
 
• They serve to anchor the organism to the substratum and absorb nutrients and water.
 
• In Polysiphonia, unicellular rhizoids help attach the prostrate filamentous section to the substratum.
 
 
 
• **Marine Algae**
 
 
• Marine algae are photosynthetic organisms found in marine environments.
 
• They include a wide variety of species, from microscopic phytoplankton to large seaweeds like kelp.
 
• Marine algae play a crucial role in oceanic ecosystems, producing oxygen and serving as the base of the marine food web.

questions.question: Which type of title can be conferred by the state as per Article 18 of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Military and Academic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 18 of the Constitution of India prohibits the state from conferring any titles except those related to Military and Academic distinctions.
 
• This provision is designed to prevent the state from granting any titles that could be seen as creating a class of nobility or honorific titles.
 
• Military titles could include ranks such as General, Colonel, etc., which are essential for the structure and functioning of the armed forces.
 
• Academic titles could include degrees such as Doctor, Professor, etc., which acknowledge educational and scholarly achievements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 18**

 
 
• Article 18 of the Indian Constitution deals with the abolition of titles.
 
• It was introduced to prevent the perpetuation of a system of titles and honors that could undermine the principles of equality enshrined in the Constitution.
 
• It states that no title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the state.
 
• It also prohibits citizens of India from accepting any title from any foreign state.
 
 
 
• **Military Titles**
 
 
• Military titles are ranks given to personnel in the armed forces as a part of their professional hierarchy.
 
• These titles signify their position, responsibilities, and authority within the military structure.
 
• Examples include ranks such as General, Major, Captain, Lieutenant, etc.
 
 
 
• **Academic Titles**
 
 
• Academic titles are conferred upon individuals in recognition of their scholarly achievements and contributions to education and research.
 
• These titles include degrees and honors such as Doctor, Professor, PhD, etc.
 
• They are essential for identifying the qualifications and expertise of individuals in academic and research institutions.

questions.question: Files and Ranks' are used in which of the following games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chess**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In chess, the board is divided into 64 squares arranged in an 8x8 grid.
 
• The vertical columns of squares are called "files" and are labeled from 'a' to 'h'.
 
• The horizontal rows of squares are called "ranks" and are numbered from 1 to 8.
 
• Each square on the chessboard is uniquely identified by a combination of its file and rank, for example, e4, d5, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chessboard Layout**

 
 
• The chessboard is a square board divided into 64 smaller squares with alternating colors (usually black and white).
 
• The squares are arranged in an 8x8 grid, where each column is referred to as a "file" and each row is referred to as a "rank".
 
 
 
• **Files and Ranks**
 
 
• Files are the vertical columns labeled 'a' to 'h' from left to right from White's perspective.
 
• Ranks are the horizontal rows numbered 1 to 8 from bottom to top from White's perspective.
 
• Each square on the board is named by its file and rank, such as 'e4', 'd5', 'a1', and 'h8'.
 
 
 
• **Chess Pieces Movement**
 
 
• Each type of chess piece moves in a specific way, and understanding the board layout of files and ranks is crucial for determining legal moves and strategies.
 
• For example, a rook moves any number of vacant squares in a file or rank, while a bishop moves diagonally any number of vacant squares.
 
 
 
• **Importance in Gameplay**
 
 
• Identifying and using files and ranks is essential for recording moves (chess notation), strategizing, and communicating positions during a game.
 
• This system of notation is universal and allows players from different languages and regions to understand and discuss chess games.

questions.question: The Swaran Singh Committee had suggested the incorporation of a total of ________ Fundamental Duties.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee was set up in 1976 to make recommendations regarding the incorporation of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The committee recommended the inclusion of 8 Fundamental Duties for citizens.
 
• These recommendations were accepted and incorporated into the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976.
 
• Initially, there were 10 Fundamental Duties listed in Part IVA (Article 51A) of the Indian Constitution, but the committee initially suggested only 8.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• They are listed in Part IVA under Article 51A.
 
• These duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and uphold the unity of India.
 
• Currently, there are 11 Fundamental Duties, but originally there were 10.

• The Human Development Report 2021-22 provides comprehensive data on various aspects of human development, including poverty.
 
• According to the report, 8.8% of the population in India is under severe multi-dimensional poverty.
 
• Multi-dimensional poverty considers various factors beyond income, such as health, education, and living standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Report (HDR)**

• The report includes the Human Development Index (HDI), which ranks countries based on these dimensions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Fundamental Duties?

options.text: They are both, civic and moral in nature.
They emphasize on respecting Indian culture.
They are not applicable to foreigners.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are justiciable.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fundamental Duties are moral obligations for every citizen of India to help promote a spirit of patriotism and uphold the unity of India.
 
• They are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning their compliance cannot be enforced by the courts.
 
• These duties emphasize respect for the Constitution, the National Flag, and the National Anthem, promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood, and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• They are mentioned in Part IVA of the Indian Constitution under Article 51A.
 
• Initially, there were 10 duties, but one more was added by the 86th Amendment Act in 2002, making the total count 11.
 
• These duties are a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they must also be conscious of their duties.
 
• Examples include respecting the national symbols, cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, and protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
 
 
• **Justiciability:**
 
 
• Justiciability refers to the ability of a subject matter to be examined and decided upon by the judiciary.
 
• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, which means they are not enforceable by law. However, if laws are made to enforce these duties, they can be justiciable.
 
• This contrasts with Fundamental Rights, which are justiciable and can be enforced by the courts.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• Also known as the "Mini-Constitution," this amendment added a new part, Part IVA, to the Constitution which lays down the Fundamental Duties of citizens.
 
• It was enacted during the Emergency period and made several changes, including the addition of the words 'Socialist,' 'Secular,' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee:**
 
 
• This committee was set up by the Government of India to make recommendations on the amendment of the Constitution.
 
• One of its key recommendations was the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution, which was accepted and implemented by the 42nd Amendment Act.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India consists of the provision for the establishment of the Finance Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 280**__.

__
 
• **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the Finance Commission.
 
• The Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India every five years or at such earlier time as he considers necessary.
 
• The main function of the Finance Commission is to make recommendations to the President on the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Centre and the States.
 
• The Finance Commission also determines the principles that should govern the grants-in-aid of the revenues of the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Finance Commission:**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body formed every five years to define the financial relations between the central government and the individual state governments.
 
• It is constituted under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The President of India appoints the Finance Commission, and it consists of a Chairman and four other members.
 
• The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are advisory in nature and are not binding on the government.
 
• The main role of the Finance Commission is to allocate a share of central taxes to the states, determine the principles for providing grants-in-aid to the states, and address any other matter referred to it by the President in the interest of sound finance.
 
 
 
• **Articles 250, 260, and 270:**
 
 
• **Article 250:** It deals with the power of Parliament to legislate with respect to any matter in the State List if a proclamation of emergency is in operation.
 
• **Article 260:** It provides that the Government of India may by agreement with any other country or territory undertake any executive, legislative, or judicial functions vested in the Government of such country or territory.
 
• **Article 270:** It deals with the taxes levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States.

• Kathakali is a major form of classical Indian dance that originated in the state of Kerala.
 
• It is known for its elaborate costumes, intricate gestures, well-defined body movements, and detailed facial expressions complemented by music and vocal performances.
 
• Kathakali is traditionally performed by male actors, who portray both male and female characters using make-up, costumes, and masks to distinguish between the various roles.
 
• The dance-drama is typically based on themes from Hindu epics like the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, as well as from the Puranas (ancient Hindu mythological texts).

• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form originating from Andhra Pradesh, not Kerala.
 
• It involves a combination of acting and dancing, and the performers often recite dialogues.
 
• Costumes and musical instruments used in Kuchipudi are similar to those in Bharatanatyam.
 
 
 
• **Bharatnatyam**
 
 
• Bharatnatyam is a classical Indian dance form that originated in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya**
 
 
• Sattriya is a classical Indian dance form that originated in Assam.
 
• It was introduced in the 15th century by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardev as a part of the neo-Vaishnavite movement.
 
• Sattriya dance is a combination of dance, drama, and music, and it is traditionally performed in Sattras (monasteries).
